column1: # Claude's two passes (QUALITY.md end) for Mi Refugio: Reina-Valera 1909 only, natural US Latin American Spanish (tú/ustedes), RV1909 name spellings, one call and response 'Dios es bueno / todo el tiempo' at the story's turn.

column3: note
column5: note

column3: Faithful to Mark 4:35-41 (4:1 for the setting); Jesus's words only as RV1909 scripture; no promised calm for the listener, only the voice that can bring it.
column5: Plain, warm Spanish an abuela would read aloud; 'Dios es bueno / todo el tiempo' tied to the storm; the night's worries named without pity.

column3: Faithful to Exod 14 (vv5-9, 15-20, 23-28 told in words); God's command to Moses told, not voiced; the pillar of cloud as the text gives it.
column5: Families, elders and children in the crossing; the people's fear understood, not mocked.

column3: Faithful to Dan 6:1-23 (vv1-9 and 11-15, 17-18 told in words); Daniel's courage credited to God as v22-23.
column5: Daily prayer honoured; natural Spanish, no Spain-only forms.

column3: Faithful to Jonah 1-3 in RV1909 versification (the fish is RV1909 2:1, the prayer 2:2-10); Nineveh's repentance (3:5-10) told in words; second chances without a promise of outcome.
column5: Warm, plain; the sailors shown with respect.

column3: Faithful to 1 Sam 17 (vv4-31, 34-36, 38-44, 48, 52 told in words); RV1909 spelling Goliath; the battle credited to the LORD as v47.
column5: Giants named as everyday fears (debt, illness, loss) without promising they fall.

column3: Faithful to Gen 37:3-28 and 39:2; Reuben (v21-22) and the second dream (v9) told in words; Gen 50:20 echoed in our own words.
column5: Family wounds named gently; no blame beyond the text.

column3: Faithful to Luke 15:11-32; the father's words as RV1909 scripture; the open ending kept as Jesus left it.
column5: Natural Spanish for a family story; the elder brother also sought, not scorned.

column3: Faithful to Ruth 1 (vv1-7, 9-13, 15, 18-19 told in words); RV1909 spellings Noemi, Ruth, Orpha, Elimelech, Booz; David and Jesus from Ruth 4 and Matt 1, stated without references.
column5: Two widows shown with dignity; Naomi's bitterness honoured, not corrected.

column3: Faithful to Dan 3 (vv1-14, 19-23, 26-27 told in words); RV1909 spellings Sadrach, Mesach, Abed-nego, Nabucodonosor; 'y si no' as the heart (v18), no promise of rescue.
column5: Courage without bravado; plain Spanish.

column3: Faithful to Mark 5:25-34 (Jairus from v22 named for the setting); the purity law named plainly, not as an attack on Judaism; no promise of healing for the listener.
column5: The woman honoured, called 'hija' as Jesus called her; her shame and courage told with care.

column3: Faithful to Gen 7:1-5, 8:6-12, 9:12-16 (the family entering from 7:7, the altar from 8:20, told in words); God's covenant read only as RV1909; the closing names God's faithfulness, no promise of an outcome for the listener.
column5: Waiting named as the listener's real life (a noticia, una respuesta); plain warm Spanish; call and response tied to the open door of the ark.

column3: Faithful to Esth 4:1-17 and 5:1-3 (Amán's decree and Esther's orphan upbringing from chs 2-3, told in words); notes God is unnamed in the book without adding doctrine; Esther's fast credited to prayer and community, not to her courage alone.
column5: RV1909 spellings kept (Esther, Mardochêo, Amán); the fear honoured; no 'you were born for this' slogan pushed on the listener.

column3: Faithful to Job 1:13-22 and 42:10-17; says plainly the restored goods are not a promise or formula and the first children did not come back; lament allowed; points to iglesia and pastor for grief.
column5: Mourning customs explained with respect; would not wound a grieving mother; Spanish an abuela would read aloud.

column3: Faithful to Gen 1:1-5 and 26-31 (days 2-5 summarised in words); imago Dei stated for every person and every skin without an ethnicity claim; no sleep promise, only rest and the returning light.
column5: Dignity of every person made explicit and gentle; natural night-time close.

column3: Faithful to John 4:5-30 (vv16-18 and 27 told in words); Jesus's words only as scripture; her past named without shaming, as the text does; 'living water' not turned into a promise.
column5: The woman is never called by a slur or pity word; the barrier between Jews and Samaritans explained plainly; she is shown as the first messenger to her town.

column3: Faithful to Matt 14:22-33 (the feeding of 14:13-21 named as setting); the fourth watch explained correctly; 'Señor, sálvame' offered as a prayer, no promise of rescue from bills or diagnosis.
column5: Peter shown with respect (the only one who stepped out); everyday troubles named without stereotype.

column3: Faithful to Exod 3:1-14 (Moses's 40 years in Midian from Acts 7:30 and Exod 2, told in words); God never voiced, YO SOY read only as scripture; 'Yo estaré contigo' quoted as God's word to Moses, then applied as presence, not an outcome.
column5: An older man called by God: speaks to elders with dignity; the desert season named kindly.

column3: Faithful to Gen 45:1-15 and 50:19-21 (Jacob's death and the brothers' fear, 50:15-18, told in words); forgiveness not rushed, harm named as real, no pressure on a hurt listener to forgive tonight.
column5: Weeping men shown with dignity; family reconciliation in natural Spanish; would comfort someone carrying an old family wound.

column3: Faithful to Luke 10:38-42; Martha not condemned for serving, as Jesus does not; the mention of Martha's faith in John 11 is scripture, not invention; no ruling on women's roles (sitting at his feet explained as a disciple's place only).
column5: Martha's tiredness recognised (cooking, children, the parents we care for) without the 'busy woman' joke; tender 'Marta, Marta'.

column3: Faithful to 1 Kgs 17:8-16 (the brook of 17:3-7 named as setting); states plainly this is not a give-to-get rule (no prosperity reading); daily bread, not a full pantry.
column5: The widow shown with dignity and faith, not as a poverty picture; a foreign widow seen by God, natural Latin American Spanish.

column3: Faithful to Gen 2:15-25 and 3:1-13 (the garments of skins, 3:21, named as later in the chapter); God never voiced; no ruling on gender roles or the fall's doctrine beyond the text; ends on God seeking, not on shame.
column5: Nakedness told plainly as the KJV/RV1909 does, nothing sexual; blame-shifting named with a gentle, human touch; natural Spanish.

column3: Faithful to 1 Sam 1:9-20 (vv1-8 and 24-28 told in words); says plainly not every prayer ends the same (no fertility promise); lament and silent prayer honoured.
column5: Childlessness handled with tenderness; the rival wife not named or mocked; would comfort a woman who has waited for a child.

column3: Faithful to Luke 19:1-10; publicans explained accurately; grace before change, restitution as fruit, salvation spoken only by Jesus in scripture.
column5: Short stature told without a joke; no 'lost cause' shaming of family members; warm close.

column3: Faithful to Mark 2:1-12; flat roofs explained; forgiveness before healing kept as the text orders it; no promise of physical healing for the listener; points to the church to carry one another.
column5: The paralysed man shown with dignity, not as a pity picture; friendship and church community honoured.

column3: Faithful to Luke 2:1-20; 'establo' tradition replaced by the text's pesebre; the angel never voiced; Mary's pondering kept.
column5: Night workers and carers named with respect; humble shepherds not romanticised; natural Christmas Spanish.

column3: Faithful to Judg 4:4-16 (the Song of Judg 5:20-21 named as scripture); Deborah's word credited to God's command; no ruling on women's leadership beyond the text; Jael's act (4:17-21) left out of a bedtime telling, battle kept off the page (violence mild).
column5: Deborah shown as wise and steady, Barak's fear without mockery; balanced for men and women listeners.

column3: Faithful to 2 Kgs 4:1-7; states it is not a debt formula or a money promise; debt-slavery custom explained; points to church and neighbours for practical help.
column5: A widowed mother shown with agency (she asks, knocks on doors) not as a poverty stereotype; no shame in asking for help.

column3: Faithful to Gen 12:1-4 and 15:1-6; faith counted as righteousness as the text says; honest lament allowed; Isaac's later birth named without a promise to the listener.
column5: An older man starting over honoured; the desert sky scene is setting only; natural Spanish.

column3: Faithful to Luke 10:25-37; priest and Levite not caricatured (the text gives no reason, and the retelling says so); the lawyer's avoidance of 'samaritano' is the text's own wording.
column5: Old enmity between peoples named plainly without blaming any modern group; invites mercy across lines; no politics.

column3: Faithful to Exod 2:1-10 (Pharaoh's order from 1:22); God not voiced; providence named without inventing speech; the mother left unnamed as in the passage.
column5: A mother, a sister and an Egyptian princess each shown with dignity and courage; Egypt named as a place, no racial label.

column3: Faithful to 1 Sam 18:1-4 and 20:35-42 (Saul's jealousy and the spear of 20:33 told in words); covenant friendship before God kept as the text frames it.
column5: The farewell kiss explained as the period's greeting between men, with no modern reading imposed; friendship honoured for any listener.

column3: Faithful to John 11:17-44; Jesus's words only as scripture; says plainly this is not a promise that our dead return tonight; an uncited 'Lazarus died again' line removed; 'resurrección y vida' left in the text, not preached as a status claim.
column5: Grief and the hospital and graveside named gently; Martha's faith honoured, Mary's tears not judged.

column3: Faithful to Judg 6:11-16 and 7:2-8 (the night attack 7:16-22 and the fleece 6:36-40 told in words, battle off the page); credits victory to God; honest doubt allowed.
column5: A frightened, poor man called 'varón esforzado' with dignity; no war glory; natural Spanish.

column3: Faithful to Mark 5:21-24 and 35-43 (the woman of 5:25-34 named as the delay); states not every sick child is healed this way (no outcome promise); Talitha cumi explained, not invented.
column5: A worried father shown with dignity; would not wound a parent who lost a child.

column3: Faithful to Gen 32:6-12 and 33:1-11 (Jacob's flight from ch 27 and the wrestling of 32:24-30 told in words); reconciliation not promised, 'no siempre depende solo de nosotros'.
column5: Family estrangement handled kindly; brothers' tears shown with dignity.

column3: Faithful to John 6:1-14 (women and children from Matt 14:21, named as setting); denarius value explained plainly; no prosperity reading of multiplication.
column5: Barley bread as the poor's bread told without pity; the unnamed boy honoured.

column3: Faithful to 1 Sam 3:1-10 (Hannah's vow from 1 Sam 1 as setting); God never voiced; no claim that God speaks to the listener tonight, only the prayer of listening.
column5: Old Eli's failures named without contempt; a child's faith shown with dignity.

column3: Faithful to 1 Kgs 3:16-28 (the dream of 3:5-12 as setting; James 1:5 alluded to, not quoted); scripture starts at v17, so the women's trade is not voiced to a bedtime listener (sexual none, as the other tellings); the death of the infant told off the page.
column5: Two poor women shown as people the king listened to; a mother's love named without sentimentality.

column3: Faithful to Mark 10:46-52; 'tu fe te ha salvado' left in scripture; no promise of healing for the listener; 'Hijo de David' explained accurately.
column5: A blind beggar shown with agency and faith, not pity; the cloak detail respectful.

column3: Faithful to Exod 19:16-20 and 20:1-17; God's words only as scripture; the day of rest told as a gift without ruling on which day (S04); grace before law, Jesus's summary from Matt 22 told in words.
column5: Former slaves given rest named with dignity; no moralising tone; natural Spanish.

column3: Faithful to Matt 25:14-29; the talent's value explained; Jesus's parable read only as scripture; faithfulness over success, no money-growth promise or prosperity reading.
column5: Gifts named in everyday church life (choir, cooking, visiting the sick); the hard ending kept without threat.

column3: Faithful to Josh 2:1-21 (her rescue in 6:22-25 and Matt 1:5 told in words); her trade named as the text names it (tag sexual: implied, adult shelf); her faith credited to what she heard of God.
column5: Rahab shown with dignity and courage, never as a joke; a foreign woman welcomed; 'nadie está demasiado lejos' kind, not shaming.

column3: Faithful to Josh 6:1-20 (the destruction of 6:21 left off the page, violence mild); obedience over method; no promise of when the listener's 'walls' fall.
column5: Waiting named gently; natural Spanish; Rahab's house remembered.

column3: Faithful to John 3:1-17 (Num 21 and John 7:50-51, 19:39 told in words); 'agua y Espíritu' left in scripture without a baptism ruling (S04); no statement of the listener's salvation status.
column5: A respected elder with questions shown with respect; doubt welcomed.

column3: Faithful to 1 Sam 25:14-35 (vv2-13 and Nabal's death in vv37-38 told in words); the crude idiom of vv22 and 34 not quoted; vengeance left to God, as v26 and v33.
column5: Abigail shown as wise, brave and humble; David corrected by a woman with no mockery of either.

column3: Faithful to 1 Kgs 19:1-15 (Carmel from ch 18 and the 7,000 of v18 told in words); Elijah's wish to die met first with rest and bread; points to 988 (oprime 2 para español), a pastor and a doctor.
column5: Burnout and despair named without shame; a strong man allowed to be tired; the crisis line given plainly in Spanish.

column3: Faithful to Mark 10:17-27 (vv28-30 summarised with the persecutions kept, no hundredfold promise); salvation as God's work; not every listener told to sell all.
column5: Wealth not mocked and poverty not romanticised; 'lo miró y lo amó' given its weight.

column3: Faithful to Gen 24:10-27 (Isaac's love, v67, told in words); v16's description of her not quoted; prayer before decisions, no promise of a spouse.
column5: Rebekah's generosity and agency honoured; the servant's worship shown; natural Spanish.

column3: Faithful to Judg 16:4-30; the blinding and the temple collapse are the KJV/RV1909's own words (tag violence: strong, adult shelf); says plainly his end is not a model for life; the hope is that he could still cry to God.
column5: Delilah shown without slurs; Samson's failure named without contempt; would not be screenshot to mock.

column3: Faithful to Matt 2:1-12 (the slaughter of 2:16 not told); the magi named as from the east without an ethnicity claim; Herod's deceit as the text implies.
column5: Speaks to immigrants with warmth ('has venido de lejos') without politics; worship before gifts.
